pair_convention.digit_index: LSD-first: index i is the coefficient of 3^i
pair_convention.alignment: LSD-align encode(x) with encode(W(x)); pad the shorter word with 0 on the MSD side
pair_convention.s_i: left_i + right_i, raw pair sum before rewrite_sum, in {-2,...,2}
pair_convention.identity: T(x)=sum_i s_i 3^i is definitional and is not a candidate

candidate_statistics.h: max {i : s_i != 0}, or None if every s_i = 0

candidate_statements.name: highest_nonzero_pair_determines_sign
candidate_statements.exact_statement: If some s_i != 0 and h=max{i:s_i!=0}, then sign(T(x))=sign(s_h). Equivalently s_h>0 implies T(x)>0 and s_h<0 implies T(x)<0
candidate_statements.motivation: Phase-6 pair-sign majority failed because counts ignore 3^i. The minimal positional repair uses only the highest nonzero pair, not the full weighted sum.
candidate_statements.relevant_domain: one-step reverse-plus-add states with at least one nonzero pair
candidate_statements.expected_yield: an exact sign(T) law from a single pair position
candidate_statements.cheapest_falsifier: the first frozen seed whose highest nonzero pair has the opposite sign of T

candidate_statements.name: highest_positive_vs_highest_negative
candidate_statements.exact_statement: If m+=max{i:s_i>0} and m-=max{i:s_i<0} are compared, then m+>m- implies T(x)>0 and m->m+ implies T(x)<0; a missing side is treated as strictly dominated
candidate_statements.motivation: The Phase-6 count comparison P+>P- failed. The natural repair compares the most significant positive position with the most significant negative position, still without the full sum.
candidate_statements.relevant_domain: one-step reverse-plus-add states with at least one nonzero pair
candidate_statements.expected_yield: an exact mixed-sign positional dominance law for sign(T)
candidate_statements.cheapest_falsifier: the first frozen seed whose higher signed position disagrees with sign(T)

candidate_statements.name: highest_mag2_determines_sign
candidate_statements.exact_statement: If h2=max{i:|s_i|=2} is defined, then sign(T(x))=sign(s_{h2}), even when a higher |s|=1 pair exists
candidate_statements.motivation: Phase 5 showed internal |s|=2 activity without length change. This tests whether the highest constructive/destructive collision captures sign, or whether a higher |s|=1 pair can dominate it.
candidate_statements.expected_yield: an exact collision-position law for sign(T)
candidate_statements.cheapest_falsifier: the first frozen seed whose highest |s|=2 pair has the opposite sign of T
candidate_statements.failure_mechanism: Highest |s|=2 pair does not determine sign: h2=1, sign(s_h2)=-1, h=2, sign(s_h)=1, 6->4.

proposals.trigger: low-information positional summaries did not close reverse-add
proposals.mathematical_target: Keep the leading reverse-add proposal on nonlinear composition of W.
proposals.mechanism: Do not register weighted_reverse_pair_interaction as a production attack.

proposals.falsifier: A reverse-add sample whose named identity fails.

proposals.trigger: positional sign laws do not explain basins
proposals.mechanism: Bounded preimage with a residue/word quotient. Do not reopen reverse_gap.
proposals.falsifier: Two predecessors indistinguishable by the quotient.
proposals.novelty_risk_reason: basin language is independent of one-step pair-position sign
